signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Sell-the-Fact
signals.text: NZD/JPY remains the focal point of G10 divergence as the pair captures both the week's strongest and weakest performers. Despite the RBNZ delivering a policy rate hike to 2.75%, the New Zealand Dollar has collapsed in a 'sell-the-fact' reaction, with NZD/USD trading at 0.5852 and the NZD G10 index down -1.405% over the last week. JPY outperformance is concurrently driven by hawkish BoJ rhetoric, with Governor Ueda stating rate hikes remain on the table for every meeting including this month's, while the TONA OIS benchmark at 0.98% keeps the JPY carry disadvantage meaningful at -177bp versus NZD. The bilateral spread of 2.387% confirms a dominant regime shift away from the NZD-carry trade. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY; aggressive sell-the-fact flow overrides the nominal rate advantage. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 75% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: Sudden risk-on impulse narrows the G10 spread below 1.20%, stabilizing NZD against the funding leg.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Complacency vs BoJ Hawkish Shift
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing 158.80, currently holding below its SMA20/50 cluster at 159.17/160.71. While the Fed-BoJ carry differential remains substantial at +270bp based on OIS (3.68% vs 0.98%), the options market exhibits unusual complacency with a VRP of -1.7% as IV at 7.2% sits below realized HV30 of 8.9%. However, the 25d risk reversal at -1.82 confirms a strong put skew, indicating that while total vol is underpriced, the demand for downside protection is intensifying following BoJ Governor Ueda's hawkish signals. Speculative positioning remains a risk factor with JPY COT LF net short at -81,619 (pctl 9), though the WoW delta of -7,978 suggests the carry-trade rebuild is meeting resistance. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; hawkish BoJ pivot threatens the crowded carry trade. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 75% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: US data surprises to the upside, widening the 10Y yield spread and reviving the carry bid.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning Extreme + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is holding at 0.7171, supported by a constructive SMA position above its 20, 50, and 200-day averages. Speculative positioning has reached a crowded extreme with COT LF net long at +53,578, placing it in the 95th percentile of its 52-week range (z-score +1.92). This institutional long bias is sharply diverged from retail sentiment, where 86% of traders are short, creating a classic contrarian setup for a retail squeeze if resistance holds. While the RBA (4.35%) vs Fed (3.75%) carry advantage of +60bp supports the bid, the crowded COT position suggests the pair is vulnerable to a 'long-unwind' if upcoming China PMIs disappoint. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; retail-short squeeze potential while holding above SMA20 at 0.7120. Catalyst: China PMI release 3 Sep. Risk: COT LF net long begins to stall alongside a close below SMA20, signaling a trend exhaustion.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Real Rate Support
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3484, currently below its SMA20 of 1.3550 but supported by the SMA50/200 cluster near 1.3444. The options market is pricing a significant risk premium with 1M IV at 11.0% versus realized HV30 of 5.0%, resulting in a massive +6.0% VRP that indicates high demand for directional protection. Despite the nominal carry being neutral at 0bp, the GBP real rate of +0.35% offers a modest restrictive cushion compared to the USD's +1.38%, keeping the pair sensitive to data surprises. COT data shows GBP longs are crowded at the 96th percentile (z +1.58), but the ESI at -9.8 suggests deteriorating macro fundamentals is likely to weigh on this speculative conviction. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; high vol premium and crowded longs suggest limited upside without a major macro catalyst. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep. Risk: A break below the 1.3440 SMA cluster triggers a large-scale liquidation of the 96th percentile long position.
